28.14.7.en: These vices and others like them, whether all of them are together in one person, or one of them rules one person and another rules another, appear in one form or another from this root, namely that they are "lovers of their own selves." This is the vice that those who shepherd the flock of Christ must guard against, lest they seek their own things and not the things of Jesus Christ, and use those for whom Christ shed His blood, using them to fulfill their own desires.

28.14.8.en: Those who shepherd His flock must have a great love, with a spiritual zeal, so that it may overcome the fear of death, which makes us (the fear of death) not desire to die so that we may live with Christ. For the Apostle Paul also desires to depart and be with Christ (Phil 1:23).

28.14.9.en: St. Augustine The prince that wanteth understanding is also a great oppressor.

28.15.0.en: He that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days [16].

28.15.1.en: When the leader turns away from the spirit of tender fatherhood, he becomes domineering and preys upon the poor flock. He behaves without understanding, for he bears the spirit of the devil, the roaring lion who walks about seeking whom he may devour (1 Pet 5:8). His rule is injustice, rapacity and the seeking of bribes, whereas he that hateth covetousness prolongs his days in goodness.

28.16.0.en: 17 A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit; let no man stay him. 18 Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved: but he that is perverse in his ways shall fall at once. 19 He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough. 20 A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent. 21 To have respect of persons is not good: for for a piece of bread that man will transgress. 22 He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him. 23 He that rebuketh a man afterwards shall find more favour than he that flattereth with the tongue. 24 Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression; the same is the companion of a destroyer. 25 He that is of a proud heart stirreth up strife: but he that putteth his trust in the LORD shall be made fat. 26 He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered. 27 He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse. 28 When the wicked rise, men hide themselves: but when they perish, the righteous increase.

28.16.1.en: A man that doeth violence to the blood of any person shall flee to the pit.

28.16.3.en: The unjust, rapacious leader forgets that the one who sheds his brother's blood, whatever his position or authority, since he has shed blood unjustly in a spirit of domination and pride, even if he flees from human judgment, will not flee from the judgment of his inner conscience, nor from the Day of Judgment. He searches for a pit to hide him, but who will hide him from his inner conscience, and who will hide him from the eyes of the Lord? Cain, the slayer of his brother, remained a fugitive, his soul never at rest, and Judas, who shed innocent blood by betrayal, found no refuge but suicide, and hanged himself.

28.16.4.en: * The devil who taught Judas to betray his Teacher turned again and taught him to hang himself, so that he might inherit by both the abyss for which he had qualified.

28.16.5.en: Darkness fears the light, and defilement dreads purity.

28.16.6.en: Why did you betray your Teacher, O Judas? And where are you going, O blind and straying one? Do you prefer sin, deceit and evil to goodness, light and faithfulness?

28.16.7.en: Will you leave your throne surrounded by light, to take a throne ablaze with fire? Do you prefer hatred to brotherhood, and leave your brethren to join those who hate you? Everyone who knew you grieves over your end and suffers.

28.16.8.en: Do you sell your Lord for a few pence, and lose the good things of earth and heaven?

28.16.9.en: What you received as the price of your treachery is not worth the price of the rope with which you will hang yourself!

28.17.0.en: St. Jacob of Serugh Whoso walketh uprightly shall be saved: but he that is perverse in his ways shall fall at once [18].

28.17.1.en: No one is perfect except God alone, but perfection here is relative; what is meant is uprightness, a sincere intention and sincerity in dealing with God and with people. One who walks in this spirit is upheld by the grace of God, who keeps him from the trials that the enemy, the devil, or people direct against him. In other words, fellowship with the holy God delivers a person in this world and in the age to come.

28.17.2.en: But the person who does not know simplicity of heart nor uprightness of conduct wavers between the ways, falls and perishes unless he returns to himself and looks to God his Savior.

28.18.0.en: He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough [19].

28.18.1.en: The wise man often repeats the exhortation to work diligently, for life has no savor without work, and has no value without diligence. Work is a divine commandment, touching our life on earth, and our reward is in heaven. We work not because we are in material need, nor to increase what we have, but because we are children of the living God, who works in love for His creation.

28.18.2.en: But the person who is lazy in his daily work, as in his spiritual conduct, is overshadowed and dominated by material and spiritual poverty.

28.18.3.en: * By our experience, by clinging to God we are able to put to death our will and cut off the desires of this world, and we learn from those who, in their relationship with God, say with all faith: "My soul followeth hard after thee" (Ps 63:8), "I have stuck unto thy testimonies: O LORD, put me not to shame" (Ps 119:31), "But it is good for me to draw near to God" (Ps 73:28). So we must not grow weary because of distraction of mind and slackness, for "He that tilleth his land shall have plenty of bread: but he that followeth after vain persons shall have poverty enough" (Prov 28:19).

28.19.0.en: Abba Serenus A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent [20].

28.19.1.en: Many consider cheating, lying, deceit and the like to be experiences a person learns in order to succeed in this life and to build up vast wealth in a short time. They consider faithfulness, honesty and exactness in conduct to be a kind of narrowness of outlook and literalism, which causes him losses and troubles. But the faithful man discovers his inner wealth, and his soul rejoices in the inheritance prepared for him, and he receives many blessings, even in this world. As for what is gathered by cheating, it will give no rest to the soul, and much will be lost in this world and in the age to come.

28.20.0.en: To have respect of persons is not good: for for a piece of bread that man will transgress [21].

28.20.1.en: For the sake of private interest, whether material or moral, a person shows partiality, and so lives without principles and belittles himself, until it brings him to act crookedly for a morsel of bread that he needs. In other words, he who shows partiality for gains that seem great will also do so for trivial matters.

28.21.0.en: He that hasteth to be rich hath an evil eye, and considereth not that poverty shall come upon him [22].

28.21.1.en: The evil eye here means the eye that has no restraint, which is never satisfied, but in greed and covetousness asks for more without stopping and without contentment. Such a person runs after material things in order to become rich, and everything flees from him, and he suffers poverty.

28.22.0.en: He that rebuketh a man afterwards shall find more favour than he that flattereth with the tongue [23].

28.22.1.en: The wise man often warns us against words of flattery that spring from a fawning heart, for they ruin both: the one who utters the flattery and the one who is puffed up by hearing it. They are words of destructive adulation. But words of rebuke that come from a faithful person and a loving heart are profitable and edifying.

28.23.0.en: Whoso robbeth his father or his mother, and saith, It is no transgression; the same is the companion of a destroyer [24].

28.23.1.en: One who squanders his parents' money, claiming that it is his right and that he is not responsible for caring for them, is a criminal against them.

28.23.2.en: This is like what some of the Pharisees permitted, that a person give from his wealth to the temple and leave his parents in need, and if anyone blamed him, he would say that what he ought to have given to them he had offered as a gift to God. The Lord Christ rebuked them, because the offering of a gift must not be at the expense of the livelihood of needy parents.

28.24.0.en: He that is of a proud heart stirreth up strife: but he that putteth his trust in the LORD shall be made fat [25].

28.24.1.en: Pride begets quarrels, for a person in his arrogance over his own opinion causes divisions. But the humble and meek person is a peacemaker for others.

28.24.2.en: Wonderfully, he sets here the one who trusts in the Lord over against the one who is of a proud heart, for none trusts in God except the one who throws himself in a spirit of humility upon the divine bosom and trusts in divine providence, and so he is satisfied with God's tenderness and mercies, and his soul is made fat.

28.24.3.en: * "Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves" (Phil 2:3)... He did not say better than yourselves, but better than themselves... What then does the Apostle mean by this? He means that we should give each one more honor, esteem and regard than he deserves... We esteem people more than they deserve... "Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus"... It is the mind of humility. "Let this mind be in you," that is, the necessity of having this mind in our life, for it is the backbone of all upright thoughts, and the only guarantee of escaping from partisanship, division, strife, conceit, pride, vainglory and self-exaltation...

28.24.4.en: Do not think of him as merely greater than you, but he is "better" than you, that is, he has a far greater loftiness, so do not be surprised or pained if you see him honored. Yes, even if he treats you with contempt, bear this nobly, since you consider him greater than yourself. And if he insults you, submit to him. And if he treats you badly, bear it in silence. For when a person is fully convinced that the other is greater than himself, he is not angry if he is treated badly, nor does he fall into envy, because he does not envy one who is far greater than himself, but ascribes everything to his loftiness.

28.25.0.en: St. John Chrysostom He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered [26].

28.25.1.en: For a person to stand alone in his opinion, not resorting to divine wisdom and not valuing the counsel, experience and wisdom of others, is folly. But whoever turns to God and seeks the counsel of others walks in safety.

28.26.0.en: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse [27].

28.26.1.en: Whoever cares for his poor brethren, God cares for him and does not leave him in want. But whoever hides his eyes from them and stops his ears to the sound of their voices will not receive a divine blessing, but the curse will come upon him.

28.26.2.en: * Do not forget this rule where it is said: "He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack." Do you forget what the Lord will say to those who give to the poor: "Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom"?

28.26.3.en: St. Augustine * If you fear and tremble lest by doing this generously your inheritance be squandered... and perhaps you will fall into poverty, do not be anxious, but take courage, for you cannot grow weary and exhausted while you perform the service of Christ, caring for a heavenly work!

28.26.4.en: I do not guarantee you, on my own responsibility, that you will not be in want; rather I promise you this relying on faith in the Holy Scriptures and on the responsibility of the divine promise.

28.26.5.en: For the Holy Spirit spoke through the mouth of Solomon, saying: "He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes shall have many a curse" (Prov 28:27), showing that the merciful and those who perform good works will not be in need, but rather whoever withholds his money, that is, the barren one, will be in need.

28.26.6.en: Add to that the saying of the blessed Apostle Paul, who was full of the grace of divine inspiration: "Now he that ministereth seed to the sower both minister bread for your food, and multiply your seed sown, and increase the fruits of your righteousness; being enriched in every thing." And also: "For the administration of this service not only supplieth the want of the saints, but is abundant also by many thanksgivings unto God" (2 Cor 9:10, 12). So while thanksgivings ascend through the prayers of the poor for our gifts and our works, our wealth increases as a reward from God.

28.27.0.en: St. Cyprian the Martyr When the wicked rise, men hide themselves: but when they perish, the righteous increase [28].

28.27.1.en: When a wicked man occupies a position of leadership, people flee for fear that evils may come upon them, and when the leadership is lost to him and is taken by a righteous man, the righteous gather around him, work with him and support him.

28.27.2.en: Let me be united with You, that I may enjoy Your righteousness!

28.27.3.en: * Whoever possesses You, O Wisdom of God, enjoys Your righteousness and walks according to Your good pleasure!

28.27.4.en: You are wisdom, virtue, goodness and peace!

28.27.5.en: * Without You evil occupies my heart, reigning and dominating with its violence and fierceness.

28.27.6.en: I do not taste the flavor of rest, nor do I find any delight in life!

28.27.7.en: * O Holy One, reign in my depths.

28.27.8.en: Then Your peace will dwell within me, and the enemy of good will not dare to creep into me.

28.27.9.en: Anxiety and turmoil cannot occupy my soul, but I will experience the pledge of Your heavens!

28.27.10.en: And my depths will rejoice in Your glories.

28.27.11.en: * Let Your peace dwell in Your Church, and pour out Your love into the hearts of mankind.

28.27.12.en: Then all will be filled with the knowledge of You, and all will experience Your peace.

28.27.13.en: * Grant me to remember Your love and Your mercy.

28.27.14.en: You, the Creator of all, became poor by Your own will, so that by Your poverty You might enrich me.

28.27.15.en: Grant me to become poor for the sake of my brethren; I desire to offer my life, poured out for all!

28.27.16.en: Grant me inner tenderness toward every person!

28.27.17.en: You have satisfied me with Your mercies.

28.27.18.en: Let me give back to You, out of what You have given me, in my brethren who are in need of You!

28.27.19.en: * You forgive me much, and in Your love You are long-suffering toward me.

28.27.20.en: You give me more than I ask and beyond what I need.

28.27.21.en: Grant me to be long-suffering toward my brethren.

28.27.22.en: Grant me to keep Your law, that I may bear witness to the divine truth, and not show partiality to an unjust man for the sake of gain.

28.27.23.en: * Let Your truth be my treasure, and Your law my wealth.

28.27.24.en: I keep Your commandment, and enjoy Your good pleasure.

28.27.25.en: * Grant me, together with truth, love and mercy.

28.27.26.en: Then I will find my delight in You, O true Love.

28.27.27.en: Grant me the spirit of knowledge and understanding, for I am indebted to You for every good thing in me!

28.27.28.en: As for my sins, I confess them to You.

28.27.29.en: I will not hide them nor justify them, that I may enjoy Your mercy, and prosper in everything.

28.27.30.en: * My depths bear witness against me because of my sins.

28.27.31.en: I do not fear a human accuser, nor the judgment of men upon me.

28.27.32.en: I fear only the corruption that creeps within me.

28.27.33.en: And my conscience that cries out within me.

28.27.34.en: Have mercy on me and forgive me, for I am a sinner!

28.27.35.en: * Grant me the spirit of uprightness and faithfulness.

28.27.36.en: Then Your grace will uphold me all the more, and keep me from all the trials of life.

28.27.37.en: Grant me simplicity of heart, that I may not waver between the ways.

28.27.38.en: * Take away from me the spirit of cheating and deceit, for I do not seek what belongs to the world but what is Yours!

28.27.39.en: I walk in the spirit of truth, and am bound only by Your good pleasure and approval.

28.27.40.en: May my eyes be satisfied by looking to You, and my heart satisfied from the treasuries of Your love!

28.27.41.en: * Let me hold to the truth for the sake of Your good pleasure; let me not show partiality to any man, nor fear anyone, but speak the truth mingled with the spirit of love.

28.27.42.en: I respect all and honor everyone, but without flattery.

28.27.43.en: * Let me hold to the spirit of meekness and humility.

28.27.44.en: So that through You I may be a peacemaker.

28.27.45.en: I flee from every atmosphere of strife.

28.27.46.en: And I find no rest in a spirit of contention.

28.27.47.en: You are our peace and the rejoicing of our hearts.
